newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Cambodians protest over strife.
newsitem.headline: Australian Cambodians protest over strife.

text.p: Cambodians in Sydney protested on Saturday over the ousting of co-premier Prince Norodom Ranarridh and urged international help to bring peace to their troubled country.
About 500 people, mainly Cambodian-Australians, demonstrated peacefully outside the Town Hall in Sydney, capital of New South Wales state.

"We wanted to voice our concern about the coup and the civil war that is going on in Cambodia," Sokhom Pech, a member of the local branch of Ranariddh's FUNCINPEC party, told the domestic news agency Australian Associated Press.
Pech urged world governments to withhold recognition of the new regime of Second Prime Minister Hun Sen, who ousted Ranariddh a week ago.
He said the protesters also wanted trade sanctions and other pressures on Hun Sen to allow Ranariddh's return and end fighting between troops loyal to the two leaders.
Australia has a standard policy of recognising countries rather than administrations.
Ranariddh and Hun Sen, head of rival parties, agreed to a coalition government after 1993 U.N.-run elections which were part of an internationally-brokered 1991 peace deal.
